_about: Generic probe payloads per vulnerability class, with an oracle that can be checked from the response alone. Arithmetic on a marker (31337+1 = 31338) is used where possible: the answer is not contained in the payload, so reflecting the input back cannot fake a hit. `variants` are other spellings of the SAME attack (alternate encodings, alternate hosts): a patch that blocks only the first spelling is overfitted, and replaying the variants is how that is caught. A variant is a string, or {value, success_if} when its oracle differs. Classes with no oracle that fits the contract are listed under `unsupported` with the reason, never silently skipped. Placeholders {OOB_URL} and {OOB_MARKER} are filled in by the runner (a loopback listener that records callbacks); the oob_marker oracle checks for the callback, so it works even when the application does not reflect the fetched body.

unsupported.sql-injection: needs a benign baseline to compare against; the replay contract has no such oracle yet
unsupported.nosql-injection: needs a benign baseline to compare against; the replay contract has no such oracle yet
unsupported.redos: needs a timing oracle, and a timing probe is itself a denial-of-service risk on a shared host
unsupported.insecure-session-cookie: checked by inspecting Set-Cookie, not by an exploit request
